hero.headline: Supreme Court declines gun industry challenge to New York liability law
hero.body:
The Supreme Court declined to hear a challenge from gun manufacturers and dealers who sought to overturn a New York state law that allows lawsuits against the firearms industry for harms caused by criminal or unlawful misuse of their products. The National Shooting Sports Foundation attempted to appeal a lower court ruling alongside Smith & Wesson and Ruger.

The New York law enables victims of gun violence and local governments to pursue civil litigation against gun manufacturers and dealers when their business practices contribute to illegal gun use. The firearms industry argued the law violates federal protections and unfairly holds them liable for criminal acts committed by third parties with their products.

By declining to hear the appeal, the Supreme Court left the lower court ruling in place, allowing the New York law to remain in effect. The justices did not issue an opinion on the merits of the constitutional questions raised by the gun industry in their challenge.

This decision represents a significant development in ongoing legal battles over gun industry liability across the country. Several states have enacted or considered similar laws in recent years, creating a patchwork of regulations governing when firearms manufacturers and sellers can be held accountable in civil court for gun violence.

The outcome of this case has broader implications for the firearms industry's legal protections. Gun manufacturers and dealers have long maintained that federal law shields them from liability when their legally sold products are misused by criminals. This argument has been central to their legal strategy in multiple jurisdictions.

Advocates for stricter gun regulations have taken the opposite position, arguing that holding the industry accountable through civil litigation provides an important tool for reducing gun violence. They contend that potential legal liability encourages safer business practices in the firearms trade and creates incentives for companies to consider how their distribution and marketing practices might contribute to illegal gun use.

The Supreme Court's decision to decline the case means the legal landscape for gun industry liability will continue to develop through state-level litigation rather than through a definitive Supreme Court ruling on the constitutional questions. This allows New York's approach to stand as a potential model for other states considering similar accountability measures.

The decision arrives as gun policy remains a contested issue in American politics and law. The contrast between the gun industry's view and that of gun safety advocates reflects deeper disagreements about corporate responsibility, constitutional protections under federal law, and the role of civil litigation in addressing public health concerns related to gun violence.

With the Supreme Court's refusal to intervene, New York's law will continue to function as written, allowing lawsuits against firearms manufacturers and dealers to proceed based on alleged connections between their business practices and unlawful gun use.

cards.headline: Eight killed in B-52 bomber crash at Edwards Air Force Base
cards.teaser: Eight Air Force personnel died when a B-52 Stratofortress bomber crashed at Edwards Air Force Base in California during a routine test mission.
cards.body:
A B-52 Stratofortress bomber crashed shortly after takeoff Monday morning at Edwards Air Force Base in California's Mojave Desert, killing all eight people on board. The aircraft was conducting a routine test mission when it went down at 11:20 a.m. Emergency response personnel responded to the scene, and officials worked to account for all personnel.

Initial indications suggest the crash was not survivable. The incident represents a significant loss for the Air Force and the surrounding community as the service investigates what caused the accident during the test flight.

cards.headline: FBI warns of security threat to Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and OneDrive users
cards.body:
The FBI issued a security warning about Kali365, a threat targeting users of Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and OneDrive. The alert, published by federal authorities, marks an urgent notice for individuals and organizations using these widely deployed Microsoft productivity applications.

Kali365 represents a security concern for the millions of people who rely on Microsoft's cloud-based collaboration and communication tools. Teams serves as a workplace chat and video platform, Outlook handles email for countless businesses and consumers, and OneDrive provides cloud storage services. The combination means the threat potentially affects a substantial portion of the American workforce and general public who use these services daily.

The FBI's decision to issue a public warning suggests the threat level warrants immediate attention from users and system administrators. Federal law enforcement typically reserves such alerts for security issues that pose significant risk or require user action to mitigate. The warning applies to anyone accessing these Microsoft services, whether through desktop applications, mobile devices, or web browsers.

Microsoft's suite of productivity tools has become fundamental infrastructure for remote work and digital collaboration, particularly since the shift to distributed work environments in recent years. Teams alone serves hundreds of millions of users globally, with a large concentration in the United States across government agencies, educational institutions, and private sector companies. OneDrive and Outlook maintain similarly broad user bases.

The timing of the FBI warning coincides with ongoing concerns about cybersecurity threats targeting widely used software platforms. Security researchers and federal agencies have repeatedly emphasized the importance of keeping software updated and following security best practices, especially for tools that handle sensitive communications and file storage. Users of the affected Microsoft services should monitor for additional guidance from both the FBI and Microsoft regarding specific protective measures or required actions.

cards.headline: San Andreas Fault reaches highest stress level in 1,000 years, study finds
cards.teaser: Research from the University of Hawai'i shows the San Andreas Fault has accumulated stress to levels not seen in a millennium.
cards.body:
The San Andreas Fault has reached its highest stress level in 1,000 years, according to a study conducted by researchers at the University of Hawai'i. The findings indicate a significant accumulation of geological pressure along the major California fault line.

The San Andreas Fault stretches roughly 800 miles through California and marks the boundary between the Pacific and North American tectonic plates. The fault system has produced major earthquakes throughout recorded history, and stress accumulation along the fault line serves as one indicator scientists use to assess seismic risk in the region.

---

Note: The additional source material provided is about different topics (fungal networks, mineral sourcing in the DRC, space telescopes, and COVID vaccines) and contains no information about the San Andreas Fault. Therefore, I've returned the original card text unchanged.

cards.headline: Trump administration bans government use of Anthropic cybersecurity models
cards.teaser: The administration forced Anthropic to remove its latest cybersecurity AI models from government use.
cards.body:
The Trump administration ordered Anthropic to withdraw its Fable and Mythos cybersecurity models from government use. Cybersecurity experts have protested the decision, arguing that restricting access to these advanced AI tools will hamper defensive security efforts and limit defenders' ability to protect software and products.

The ban reflects broader shifts in how the Trump administration is managing AI across federal agencies. Government AI use has expanded significantly, with over 3,600 active or planned AI applications now deployed across federal agencies—a 70% increase from the Biden administration's final year. These implementations extend to sensitive functions including public health, nuclear safety, and individual rights determinations.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans seek role in reviewing Trump Iran agreement
cards.teaser: Republican lawmakers said they want to examine the details of any final deal, though overturning an agreement faces a high legal threshold.
cards.body:
Senate Republicans want to review the details of President Trump's Iran peace agreement. Lawmakers said they are eager to examine the fine print of any final deal, though they acknowledged a high bar exists for overturning an agreement reached by the administration.

The push reflects broader tensions between Congress and the executive branch over foreign policy authority and the role of lawmakers in approving international agreements. Trump has already announced a deal to end the war with Iran, with French President Emmanuel Macron congratulating him on the agreement at the G7 summit in France.

cards.headline: Russian attack in Ukraine kills 11 and damages historic cathedral
cards.teaser: A Russian barrage struck multiple locations in Ukraine, setting fire to a landmark cathedral and killing at least 11 people.
cards.body:
Russian forces launched strikes across Ukraine, resulting in at least 11 deaths. The barrage of drones and missiles targeted Kyiv and other locations throughout the country, striking the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra monastery complex, one of Ukraine's most significant religious and cultural landmarks. The cathedral caught fire during the attack.

The monastery has long served as an important site for worship and tourism before the war. The attack represents another instance of cultural heritage sites sustaining damage amid the ongoing conflict.

hero.body:

cards.headline: Eight crew members killed in B-52 bomber crash in California
cards.teaser: A US Air Force B-52 bomber crashed during a routine test mission, killing all eight people on board.
cards.body:
An Air Force B-52 Stratofortress crashed shortly after takeoff on Monday morning at Edwards Air Force Base in California's Mojave Desert. All eight people aboard the aircraft, which was on a routine test mission, are presumed dead. The crash occurred at 11:20 a.m.

Emergency response personnel responded to the scene. Air Force officials indicated that the crash was not survivable based on initial assessments.

cards.headline: Bank of Japan raises interest rates to highest level since 1995
cards.teaser: Japan's central bank continued its policy shift away from near-zero rates, pushing borrowing costs to levels not seen in three decades.
cards.body:
The Bank of Japan raised its benchmark interest rate to the highest level since 1995, continuing its shift away from the near-zero rate environment that dominated Japanese monetary policy for decades. The central bank has been gradually increasing rates from near-zero starting in 2024.

This policy transformation reflects Japan's changing economic conditions and marks a significant departure from the ultra-loose monetary approach the country long maintained.

cards.headline: Philippines earthquake raised seabed by up to two meters
cards.teaser: The deadly earthquake that struck the southern Philippines was found to have lifted portions of the ocean floor by as much as two meters.
cards.body:
Scientists examining the aftermath of the 7.8 magnitude earthquake that struck southern Mindanao on Monday found that the seabed rose by as much as 2 metres in some areas. This "coastal uplift" exposed coral and damaged marine life, while residents reported that shorelines extended by up to 200 metres.

The deadly quake killed at least 61 people, with at least 40 others still missing according to the country's disaster agency. The Philippines' environment department confirmed the significant seabed changes resulting from the powerful seismic event.

cards.headline: Australia to investigate assault allegations by Gaza flotilla activists
cards.teaser: Australian authorities will examine claims by activists that they were assaulted after being detained by Israeli forces in May.
cards.body:
Australia has launched an investigation into allegations from activists who participated in a Gaza flotilla that they were kidnapped, raped, and tortured while in Israeli custody. The activists were detained by Israeli forces in May during an attempted maritime journey to Gaza.

The probe follows formal complaints filed by Australian citizens who claimed they were subjected to serious assaults while being held. Israeli forces have previously intercepted flotilla attempts aimed at breaking the naval blockade of Gaza.

cards.headline: Trust in news reaches record low, research shows
cards.teaser: The Reuters Institute recorded its lowest levels of public trust in news media since it began tracking the metric in 2015.
cards.body:
Trust in news organizations has fallen to its lowest level since the Reuters Institute began tracking the metric in 2015. The decline reflects a sustained erosion of public confidence in journalism and media outlets across multiple countries.

The downward trend demonstrates a fundamental shift in how audiences view news sources rather than a temporary dip in confidence. This sustained decline raises questions about the future relationship between the public and traditional media institutions.

cards.headline: California governor says justice department investigating wife and former staff
cards.teaser: Governor Gavin Newsom alleged that federal investigators have been examining his wife and ex-staff members for roughly a year.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

California Governor Gavin Newsom stated that the Justice Department is conducting investigations involving his wife and former staff members. A source familiar with the matter confirmed that the investigations have been underway for approximately one year.

Newsom made the allegations public amid what appears to be ongoing federal scrutiny of individuals connected to his administration. The governor's public statement marks a rare acknowledgment of federal investigations touching his inner circle.

---

Note: The source material provided does not contain substantive details about the investigations themselves—only headline references and unrelated content about other DOJ matters. The original card text already represents the confirmed facts available. No rewrite is warranted without additional sourced details about the scope, subjects, or nature of these investigations.

hero.headline: Eight killed in B-52 bomber crash at Edwards Air Force Base
hero.teaser: Eight Air Force personnel died when a B-52 Stratofortress bomber crashed at Edwards Air Force Base in California during a routine test mission.
hero.body:
A B-52 Stratofortress bomber crashed shortly after takeoff Monday morning at Edwards Air Force Base in California's Mojave Desert, killing all eight people on board. The aircraft was conducting a routine test mission when it went down at 11:20 a.m. Emergency response personnel responded to the scene, and officials worked to account for all personnel.

Initial indications suggest the crash was not survivable. The incident represents a significant loss for the Air Force and the surrounding community as the service investigates what caused the accident during the test flight.

cards.headline: G7 leaders begin summit talks in France
cards.teaser: Leaders of the Group of Seven nations have opened summit discussions focused on Ukraine and the Middle East.
cards.body:
G7 leaders have gathered in France to discuss the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East. The summit follows President Trump's announcement of an agreement to end the U.S. conflict with Iran.

The Iranian conflict has recently taken center stage in international diplomatic discussions, overshadowing attention on Ukraine. French President Emmanuel Macron met with Trump and congratulated him on the new Iran agreement.

cards.headline: Kennedy Center removes Trump name from building
cards.teaser: The Kennedy Center has taken down Donald Trump's name from the building, with a tarp now covering the exterior.
cards.body:
The Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts has removed President Trump's name from the building following a court order. A tarp now covers the exterior where the name was previously displayed.

The cultural institution has not yet revealed plans for the building's appearance going forward, leaving the temporary covering in place as it determines next steps for the facade.

cards.headline: Alaska official bars second Dan Sullivan from Senate race
cards.teaser: A candidate with the same name as Alaska's sitting senator has been ruled ineligible for the ballot.
cards.body:
Alaska's elections chief has disqualified a second candidate named Dan Sullivan from the Republican Senate primary ballot. Daniel J Sullivan Jr., a former teacher, had filed to run against incumbent Senator Dan S Sullivan, creating a naming conflict in the high-stakes race.

Republicans filed complaints alleging that the other Dan Sullivan coordinated with a Democratic campaign to confuse voters. Election officials determined his candidacy was filed with intent to mislead the electorate. Senator Dan Sullivan will be the only candidate by that name appearing on the ballot.

cards.headline: Washington holds primary elections for delegate and mayor
cards.teaser: The District of Columbia conducted primary elections for its U.S. delegate and mayoral races.
cards.body:
Washington voters cast ballots in primary elections to select nominees for the U.S. delegate seat and mayor of the District of Columbia. The primaries determine which candidates will advance to the general election later in the year.

The delegate position represents the District in the House of Representatives, though the seat does not have full voting rights on legislation. The mayoral race will determine who leads the city government for the next term. Results from the primary elections are being tabulated and reported.

cards.headline: Vance describes Vatican meeting as unsettling in new book
cards.teaser: Vice President Vance has written about his Catholic faith and past comments in a newly published book.
cards.body:
Vice President J.D. Vance has published a new book centered on his Catholic faith and its influence on his personal life and political views. He characterizes a Vatican meeting from the previous year as unsettling but does not elaborate on specifics.

In the book, Vance reflects on earlier controversial remarks, describing his "childless cat ladies" comment as among the most regrettable statements he has made. The work examines his religious conversion and the role faith plays in shaping his worldview.

cards.headline: UFC chief says White House fight night will not be repeated
cards.teaser: Dana White says the UFC will not hold another event at a federal landmark after logistical challenges with Freedom 250.
cards.body:
UFC president Dana White has ruled out holding another fight event at the White House, declaring "never again" to similar events at federal landmarks.

The decision comes after Freedom 250 presented significant operational challenges. White cited weather concerns from the outdoor venue, the complexity of constructing the octagon cage, and substantial costs associated with staging events at federal properties as factors making future White House fights impractical. The event will remain a one-time occurrence rather than establishing a new tradition.

hero.headline: China's Consumer Spending Falls for First Time Since Pandemic
hero.body:
China's retail sales declined unexpectedly in May, marking the first drop in consumer spending since the COVID-19 pandemic ended. The contraction signals deepening economic weakness as Chinese households reduce discretionary purchases amid persistent economic uncertainty. The decline in domestic consumption highlights the country's growing dependence on exports to maintain economic growth.

The retail sales data showed spending and investment falling to levels not seen since the pandemic era, according to official economic statistics. The unexpected downturn caught economists off guard, as forecasts had anticipated continued modest growth in consumer activity. The spending pullback reflects household caution as economic conditions remain uncertain.

The weakening domestic demand comes as China faces mounting pressure to stimulate its economy through policy measures. With consumers tightening their belts, the country's economic model has shifted toward greater reliance on international trade to offset sluggish internal consumption. This imbalance raises concerns about the sustainability of China's economic growth trajectory.

The May data underscores the challenges facing Chinese policymakers as they attempt to revive consumer confidence and domestic spending. Investment figures also registered significant declines, compounding concerns about the economy's near-term prospects. The simultaneous contraction in both consumption and investment suggests broader structural issues beyond temporary market fluctuations.

The economic slowdown carries implications for global markets, as China remains a major engine of worldwide economic activity. The country's shift toward export-driven growth amid weak domestic demand could intensify trade tensions and affect supply chains globally. Chinese authorities face difficult choices in balancing economic stimulus measures against long-term financial stability concerns.

cards.headline: Bank of Japan Raises Interest Rates to Highest Level Since 1995
cards.teaser: Japan's central bank increased rates to a 31-year high amid currency pressures and inflation from energy disruptions.
cards.body:
The Bank of Japan has raised interest rates to their highest point since 1995, marking a significant policy shift. The central bank has been gradually increasing rates from near-zero levels starting in 2024. The decision came despite opposition from Prime Minister Takaichi and reflected responses to U.S. pressure, a weakening yen at historic lows, and inflation stemming from global energy market disruptions.

The rate increase is intended to support the yen and address inflationary pressures. However, the yen showed limited immediate response to the move, continuing to trade near historic lows against the dollar.

cards.headline: UK Government Blocks Thames Water Rescue Deal Over Consumer Protections
cards.teaser: Thames Water moved closer to potential nationalization after the government rejected a proposed rescue package.
cards.body:
The UK government has rejected a proposed rescue package for Thames Water, citing inadequate protections for consumers and the environment. The decision moves the struggling utility company closer to potential nationalization.

Thames Water has faced serious financial and operational challenges, prompting discussions about its future. The government's objection to the private rescue deal signals a shift toward greater state involvement in the company's operations.

cards.headline: General Motors in Talks to Manufacture Weapons Components for Lockheed Martin
cards.teaser: The automaker is negotiating to supply weapons parts to the defense contractor.
cards.body:
General Motors entered discussions with Lockheed Martin about supplying components for weapons manufacturing. The negotiations represent a potential expansion of GM's business into defense contracting. The talks indicate growing collaboration between traditional automotive manufacturers and defense industry companies.

The partnership discussions come as defense contractors seek to expand their supply chains and manufacturing capacity. GM's industrial capabilities and production infrastructure could provide Lockheed Martin with additional manufacturing resources. The arrangement would mark a significant diversification of GM's product portfolio beyond automotive applications.

cards.headline: Microsoft Turns to Amazon Cloud Services for GitHub Capacity Issues
cards.teaser: The company is using its biggest cloud competitor to address AI-driven strains on GitHub.
cards.body:
Microsoft began utilizing Amazon Web Services to manage capacity pressures on GitHub driven by artificial intelligence workloads. The move represents an unusual step of turning to its primary cloud computing rival to address infrastructure challenges. GitHub has experienced availability issues as AI-related usage surged beyond existing capacity.

The capacity strains forced Microsoft to seek additional cloud resources beyond its own Azure infrastructure. The decision highlights the scale of demand created by AI applications on code-sharing platforms. Microsoft's reliance on a competitor's infrastructure underscores the technical challenges of managing rapid AI adoption.

cards.headline: White House Dispute with Anthropic Over AI Model Continues
cards.teaser: The administration maintains restrictions on Anthropic's flagship AI product amid ongoing tensions.
cards.body:
Anthropic suspended its newly released AI models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, following a June 12th government order to block foreign access. The White House raised cybersecurity and hacking concerns about the tools, which had launched publicly just days earlier on June 9th.

The dispute adds to existing tensions between Anthropic and the U.S. government, including a separate standoff with the Pentagon. The company's decision to suspend the models reflects the regulatory pressures facing AI developers navigating national security considerations.

cards.headline: Helium-3 Mining Plans Target Moon as Demand Forecast to Rise
cards.teaser: The rare isotope's high cost and expected demand increase are driving lunar extraction proposals.
cards.body:
Helium-3, a rare and expensive isotope, faces soaring demand projections that have prompted proposals to mine the material on the moon. The element commands high prices due to its scarcity on Earth and specialized applications. Industry forecasts predict substantial increases in helium-3 requirements in coming years.

Some companies are developing plans to extract helium-3 from lunar surface materials where the isotope exists in greater concentrations. The moon's regolith contains helium-3 deposited by solar winds over billions of years. Mining operations would require significant technological development and infrastructure investment to become commercially viable.

cards.headline: Nintendo releases Switch and Switch 2 system update version 22.5.0
cards.teaser: Nintendo issued firmware update 22.5.0 for both the original Switch and Switch 2 consoles.
cards.body:
Nintendo released system software version 22.5.0 for the Switch and Switch 2 gaming consoles. The update adds support for additional languages and includes a dark mode option for the Switch eShop digital storefront.

The firmware update applies to both console generations, with the Switch 2 receiving language support expansion. Nintendo replaced the eShop interface on the original Switch as part of the update. The patch is available for download now through the consoles' system settings.

cards.headline: Google Earth flight simulator now available in web browsers
cards.teaser: Google launched a browser-based version of its Google Earth flight simulator, eliminating the need for high-end computer hardware.
cards.body:
Google Earth's flight simulator feature is now accessible directly through web browsers. The tool previously required users to download the Google Earth application, but the browser version allows anyone with an internet connection to pilot virtual aircraft around the world.

The simulator lets users fly over Google Earth's three-dimensional mapping data without installing software or owning powerful computer hardware. Users can navigate the flight controls directly from their web browser to explore aerial views of global terrain and landmarks.

cards.headline: NASA prepares Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope for launch
cards.teaser: NASA's upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will operate 1,000 times faster than the Hubble Space Telescope.
cards.body:
NASA is preparing to launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, an observatory designed to survey the universe at speeds far exceeding the Hubble Space Telescope. The Roman telescope will operate 1,000 times faster than Hubble, allowing it to map large portions of space in significantly less time.

The telescope uses technology originally developed for spy satellites to observe distant cosmic phenomena. NASA opened a campaign inviting the public to submit their names to be included aboard the spacecraft. The mission aims to study dark energy, exoplanets, and other astronomical targets with unprecedented efficiency.

cards.headline: Microsoft reportedly considers closing Xbox game studios
cards.teaser: Microsoft's Xbox division is weighing studio closures, including Compulsion Games, Double Fine, and Ninja Theory.
cards.body:
Microsoft closes Xbox studio Ninja Theory

Microsoft has shut down Ninja Theory, the studio behind the Hellblade series. Staff were informed of the closure during a Monday call, though the studio hopes to find a buyer.

The shutdown is part of a broader restructuring of Xbox's development operations. Compulsion Games and Double Fine are also among several Xbox studios facing closure as Microsoft reassesses its gaming division.

cards.headline: Gemini experiences service disruption on Android and Android Auto
cards.teaser: Google's Gemini AI assistant stopped making calls on Android devices and Android Auto for some users.
cards.body:
Google Gemini experienced an outage affecting its ability to make phone calls on Android smartphones and Android Auto systems. Users encountered error messages stating something went wrong when attempting to use the voice assistant for calling functions.

Google acknowledged the service disruption as reports of the problem spread across social media and user forums. The company indicated it was working to restore full functionality to the AI assistant. The outage impacted users who rely on Gemini for hands-free calling, particularly those using Android Auto while driving.

hero.headline: Pete Crow-Armstrong hits first cycle of 2026 season
hero.body:
Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong became the first player in Major League Baseball to hit for the cycle this season. The achievement marks a milestone in what has been a breakout campaign for the young outfielder.

Hitting for the cycle requires a batter to record a single, double, triple, and home run in the same game. The feat is considered one of baseball's rarest accomplishments, occurring far less frequently than a no-hitter. Crow-Armstrong joins an exclusive group of Cubs players to achieve the cycle in franchise history.

The 22-year-old has emerged as a key player for Chicago this season after being acquired in a trade with the New York Mets in 2021. Originally drafted 19th overall by the Mets in 2020, Crow-Armstrong moved through the Cubs farm system and made his major league debut last year. His combination of speed and defensive ability in center field has made him a regular in the Cubs lineup.

Crow-Armstrong's performance comes as the Cubs work to build around a young core of position players. The team has invested heavily in player development in recent years, with several homegrown talents now contributing at the major league level. His ability to impact games both offensively and defensively has made him a cornerstone of the organization's plans moving forward.

The cycle represents the kind of all-around offensive production that Cubs management envisioned when they committed to Crow-Armstrong as their starting center fielder. With more than half the season remaining, his emergence provides Chicago with another dimension in their lineup as they compete in the National League Central Division.

cards.headline: Brendan Sorsby plans to enter NFL supplemental draft
cards.teaser: Texas Tech transfer quarterback Brendan Sorsby will apply for the NFL's supplemental draft amid legal disputes over his NCAA eligibility.
cards.body:
Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby plans to apply for the NFL's supplemental draft amid ongoing NCAA eligibility disputes. His decision comes after betting admissions sparked controversy during the offseason, with the Big 12 and NCAA challenging his eligibility status.

The supplemental draft allows players to enter the NFL after missing the regular draft deadline or facing college eligibility issues. Sorsby had until June 22 to submit his application. Teams bidding for supplemental draft picks must forfeit a corresponding selection in the following year's regular draft.

cards.headline: James Dolan urged Knicks to sacrifice for title run
cards.teaser: Knicks owner James Dolan delivered a speech before the playoffs asking players to give everything in pursuit of a championship.
cards.body:
New York Knicks owner James Dolan delivered an impassioned speech to his team before the playoffs, asking players to make significant sacrifices during their championship push. Invoking the example of Spartans, Dolan urged the team to abstain from sex for approximately 10 weeks—the length of a full playoff run.

The strategy appeared to work. The Knicks won their first NBA championship in 53 years, ending a historic drought. The title was fueled by Jalen Brunson's stellar play, coach Mike Brown's leadership, a suffocating defense, and a healthy roster at the right time.

cards.headline: Iran forced to leave Los Angeles after World Cup opener
cards.teaser: Iran's national team was required to return to their base camp in Mexico immediately after their opening World Cup match in Los Angeles.
cards.body:
Iran drew 2-2 with New Zealand in their World Cup opener in Los Angeles, but the match was overshadowed by restrictions placed on the team. Coach Amir Ghalenoei called Iran the "most oppressed" team at the tournament after being forced to return to their base in Tijuana, Mexico immediately following the game. A charter flight from LAX was scheduled for 11pm local time.

The team's participation has been marked by unusual complications throughout their preparation. FIFA president Gianni Infantino visited the Iranian dressing room after the match to hear the team's concerns. Captain Mehdi Taremi described their World Cup experience as a "disaster," citing the logistical and political challenges surrounding their campaign.

cards.headline: MLB criticizes Bible verses on Pride Night hats
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball condemned personal writings on team-issued Pride Night hats after San Francisco Giants players added Bible verses.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball criticized the San Francisco Giants for adding Bible verses to Pride Night caps worn during Friday's game against the Chicago Cubs. MLB issued a statement Monday opposing personal writings on team-issued specialty caps used for Pride Night celebrations.

The league's stance applies to all personal messages and religious texts on such caps, regardless of intent. MLB emphasized that team-issued Pride Night merchandise should remain unaltered.

cards.headline: Calvin Johnson expects Puka Nacua to break receiving record
cards.teaser: The former Lions receiver believes his single-season yardage record will fall soon, with the Rams star as the top candidate.
cards.body:
Calvin Johnson said he does not expect his single-season NFL record for receiving yards to last much longer. The former Detroit Lions star identified Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua as the most likely player to break the mark.

Johnson set the record during his playing career with the Lions. Nacua emerged as one of the league's most productive receivers, posting impressive yardage totals that have positioned him as a threat to surpass Johnson's benchmark in the coming seasons.

cards.headline: Tom Izzo calls for alumni action on Michigan State changes
cards.teaser: The longtime basketball coach expressed displeasure with leadership changes at Michigan State and urged alumni to intervene.
cards.body:
Michigan State basketball coach Tom Izzo said he was disgusted by the leadership changes taking place around him at the university. Izzo, who has coached the Spartans for decades, made a public call for the school's alumni to take action.

Izzo's comments reflect tensions between the basketball program and university administration over recent personnel decisions. The coach's appeal to alumni represents an unusual public challenge to the direction of Michigan State's athletic department leadership.

hero.headline: Country Singer Jelly Roll Files for Divorce From Wife Bunnie Xo
hero.body:
Country music artist Jelly Roll has filed for divorce from his wife Bunnie Xo, ending a marriage that began in Las Vegas in 2016. The filing marks a significant personal development for the singer, who has risen to prominence in country music in recent years.

Bunnie Xo, whose legal name is Bunnie DeFord, is known for her work as an adult content creator and podcast host. The couple married ten years ago in Las Vegas and have been public figures in their respective entertainment fields. Jelly Roll, born Jason DeFord, has built a successful career blending country, hip-hop, and rock influences.

The divorce filing comes as Jelly Roll continues to maintain a busy touring and recording schedule. He has become one of country music's most recognizable artists, known for songs that often address personal struggles and redemption. His career trajectory has included multiple award nominations and chart success over the past several years.

Bunnie Xo has built her own platform through podcasting and social media, where she has discussed various aspects of their relationship and personal lives over the years. The couple had been open about their relationship in public forums, making the divorce filing a notable shift from their previously public partnership.

Neither Jelly Roll nor Bunnie Xo has released a public statement about the divorce filing. The legal proceedings are expected to unfold in the coming months. The split affects both their personal lives and their public personas, as both have cultivated audiences that followed their relationship as part of their public identities.

cards.headline: Jon Stewart Criticizes UFC Fighter for Comments About Michelle Obama
cards.teaser: The Daily Show host responded to remarks made by fighter Josh Hokit during a post-fight interview at a White House UFC event.
cards.body:
Jon Stewart criticized UFC fighter Josh Hokit on Monday's episode of The Daily Show for offensive comments made during a post-fight interview at UFC Freedom 250. The event, held on the White House South Lawn on Sunday night, marked an unusual venue for mixed martial arts competition under the Trump administration.

During his post-fight remarks, Hokit made disparaging comments about former First Lady Michelle Obama, claiming she "is a man." Stewart responded sharply on air, calling Hokit a "f—ing a–hole" for the remarks. The event also drew criticism from musician Sheryl Crow, who condemned the Trump administration for staging the UFC fights at the White House, calling it "disgraceful and void of decency."

cards.headline: Sheryl Crow Criticizes White House UFC Event
cards.teaser: The singer-songwriter called the Trump administration's hosting of UFC Freedom 250 at the White House disgraceful.
cards.body:
Sheryl Crow posted criticism of the UFC Freedom 250 event held at the White House, calling it disgraceful and void of decency. The singer-songwriter shared her response on Instagram Stories, continuing her pattern of speaking out against President Donald Trump's actions.

The outdoor event on the White House lawn proved logistically challenging and expensive to produce. According to UFC boss Dana White, the show will not be repeated, citing weather concerns, construction complications for the cage and staging, and the high costs associated with hosting fights at federal landmarks.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Restaurants Win Multiple James Beard Awards
cards.teaser: The city's culinary scene received recognition at the 2026 James Beard Awards ceremony.
cards.body:
Los Angeles restaurants and chefs received multiple honors at the 2026 James Beard Awards, one of the culinary industry's most prestigious recognition programs. The awards ceremony highlighted the city's diverse food scene and recognized achievements in various categories.

The James Beard Awards honor excellence in the restaurant and food industry across the United States. This year's ceremony also saw wins from chefs and restaurants in Philadelphia, San Francisco, and Chicago, including Jesse Ito of Royal Sushi & Izakaya in Philadelphia and Jacob Potashnick of Feld in Chicago.

cards.headline: Trust in News Media Reaches Lowest Level Since 2015
cards.teaser: Annual research from the Reuters Institute shows trust in news has declined to its lowest point in the study's history.
cards.body:
The Reuters Institute has recorded its lowest trust figures in news media since beginning its annual research in 2015. The findings represent a continued decline in public confidence in news organizations and journalism across multiple countries.

The annual study tracks public attitudes toward news media and consumption patterns. The latest results show a marked decrease from previous years, indicating growing skepticism among audiences about news sources and reporting. The research provides insight into how audiences engage with and perceive news organizations.

cards.headline: Judge Orders Justin Baldoni to Pay Blake Lively's Legal Fees
cards.teaser: The ruling comes as the legal dispute between the It Ends With Us co-stars nears conclusion.
cards.body:
A judge has ordered Justin Baldoni to pay Blake Lively's legal fees in their ongoing dispute. The ruling represents a partial victory for Lively as the legal proceedings related to the film It Ends With Us approach resolution.

The case has drawn attention throughout the entertainment industry as both actors were involved in the production of It Ends With Us. Legal analysts have noted that Lively made a calculated decision on her legal strategy. The settlement terms have been published by Baldoni's lawyer, indicating the case may be moving toward final resolution.

cards.headline: New York Knicks Players Appear on The Tonight Show After Championship Win
cards.teaser: Point guard Jalen Brunson and teammates celebrated their NBA championship victory with host Jimmy Fallon.
cards.body:
Members of the New York Knicks visited The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon to celebrate their NBA championship victory, the franchise's first title in 53 years. Point guard Jalen Brunson reflected on the team's playoff run, describing how the players fought back through challenging games and persevered together.

Brunson acknowledged that winning the championship still felt surreal. During the appearance, he shared the emotional journey of the team's journey and expressed gratitude for what the victory meant to the organization and its fans.

hero.headline: Supreme Court declines gun industry challenge to New York liability law
hero.body:
The Supreme Court declined to hear a challenge from gun manufacturers and dealers who sought to overturn a New York state law that allows lawsuits against the firearms industry for harms caused by criminal or unlawful misuse of their products. The National Shooting Sports Foundation attempted to appeal a lower court ruling alongside Smith & Wesson and Ruger.

The New York law enables victims of gun violence and local governments to pursue civil litigation against gun manufacturers and dealers when their business practices contribute to illegal gun use. The firearms industry argued the law violates federal protections and unfairly holds them liable for criminal acts committed by third parties with their products.

By declining to hear the appeal, the Supreme Court left the lower court ruling in place, allowing the New York law to remain in effect. The justices did not issue an opinion on the merits of the constitutional questions raised by the gun industry in their challenge.

This decision represents a significant development in ongoing legal battles over gun industry liability across the country. Several states have enacted or considered similar laws in recent years, creating a patchwork of regulations governing when firearms manufacturers and sellers can be held accountable in civil court for gun violence.

The outcome of this case has broader implications for the firearms industry's legal protections. Gun manufacturers and dealers have long maintained that federal law shields them from liability when their legally sold products are misused by criminals. This argument has been central to their legal strategy in multiple jurisdictions.

Advocates for stricter gun regulations have taken the opposite position, arguing that holding the industry accountable through civil litigation provides an important tool for reducing gun violence. They contend that potential legal liability encourages safer business practices in the firearms trade and creates incentives for companies to consider how their distribution and marketing practices might contribute to illegal gun use.

The Supreme Court's decision to decline the case means the legal landscape for gun industry liability will continue to develop through state-level litigation rather than through a definitive Supreme Court ruling on the constitutional questions. This allows New York's approach to stand as a potential model for other states considering similar accountability measures.

The decision arrives as gun policy remains a contested issue in American politics and law. The contrast between the gun industry's view and that of gun safety advocates reflects deeper disagreements about corporate responsibility, constitutional protections under federal law, and the role of civil litigation in addressing public health concerns related to gun violence.

With the Supreme Court's refusal to intervene, New York's law will continue to function as written, allowing lawsuits against firearms manufacturers and dealers to proceed based on alleged connections between their business practices and unlawful gun use.

cards.headline: Lawmakers warn Interior officials they lack authority to build Trump arch
cards.teaser: Six members of Congress sent a letter stating that the Interior Department and National Park Service cannot construct a triumphal arch without congressional approval.
cards.body:
Six lawmakers sent a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and Acting Director of the National Park Service Jessica Bowron asserting that the officials have no authority to build a triumphal arch without approval from Congress. The letter stated that the lawmakers oppose the project in the strongest terms.

The communication represents congressional pushback against an apparent administration plan to construct the monument. The lawmakers' letter emphasizes the constitutional separation of powers and Congress's role in authorizing major construction projects on federal land and at national monuments.

cards.headline: Trump administration considered export controls on Anthropic before forcing AI model offline
cards.teaser: The White House weighed export restrictions on the AI company weeks before shutting down its flagship product over a dispute about technology sharing with a China-linked firm.
cards.body:
The Trump administration contemplated imposing export controls on Anthropic in the weeks leading up to forcing the company's AI model offline. The action followed a dispute over Anthropic's sharing of technology with a firm connected to China.

The sequence of events illustrates tensions between the administration and the artificial intelligence company over national security concerns related to technology transfer. The decision to take the AI model offline represented a significant escalation in the conflict between the White House and Anthropic over the company's business relationships and technology-sharing practices.

cards.headline: California governor says Justice Department opened investigation into him
cards.teaser: Gavin Newsom announced that the U.S. Department of Justice has launched an investigation into him and his wife.
cards.body:
California Governor Gavin Newsom announced that the U.S. Department of Justice has opened an investigation into him and his wife, Jennifer Siebel Newsom. In a video statement, Newsom claimed that President Trump directed the DOJ to target him, allegedly because of his potential presidential ambitions.

The investigation is the latest allegation from a Trump political opponent claiming the administration has weaponized the Justice Department. It reflects escalating tensions between the Trump administration and Democratic governors who have emerged as vocal critics of federal policies.

cards.headline: Trump disputes reports of $300 billion Iran reconstruction fund
cards.teaser: President Trump called reports of a major reconstruction fund for Iran as part of a peace agreement "Fake News."
cards.body:
President Trump denied reports that Iran would receive $300 billion in reconstruction funding under a peace agreement with the United States. Trump said Iran has committed to never acquiring nuclear weapons and characterized the financial arrangement story as inaccurate.

According to Vice President Vance, the U.S.-Iran deal is roughly a page and a half long and described as "very general," with many details to be negotiated later. Senate Republicans have indicated they want to review the agreement's specifics, though they face a high threshold for overturning any final deal.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans seek role in reviewing Trump Iran agreement
cards.teaser: Republican lawmakers said they want to examine the details of any final deal, though overturning an agreement faces a high legal threshold.
cards.body:
Senate Republicans want to review the details of President Trump's Iran peace agreement. Lawmakers said they are eager to examine the fine print of any final deal, though they acknowledged a high bar exists for overturning an agreement reached by the administration.

The push reflects broader tensions between Congress and the executive branch over foreign policy authority and the role of lawmakers in approving international agreements. Trump has already announced a deal to end the war with Iran, with French President Emmanuel Macron congratulating him on the agreement at the G7 summit in France.

cards.headline: Green algae reappear in reflecting pool despite Trump renovation
cards.teaser: Algae returned to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool just days after renovations that included technology designed to eliminate the growth.
cards.body:
Green algae have returned to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on the National Mall despite President Trump's renovations of the site. The project cost more than $13 million and included the addition of nanobubbler technology that has successfully destroyed algae, according to the Interior Department.

Images showed the algae had reappeared at the site shortly after the renovation work was completed. An Interior Department spokesperson provided comment to The Hill about the technology that had been installed as part of the extensive refurbishment project at the iconic Washington landmark.
